mantra.line: The loop already runs at full speed — boresight, how-copy, build, FRAGO, in one breath. Naming it costs nothing it isn't already spending.
One question is open: design process, or software life cycle. Answer it once, in one document, beside the project flow — not re-litigated across BOLOs.
Call it what 12207 and 15288 call it — the iterative life-cycle model — and take credit for having built it before it had a name.

frago.mission: Write the Command's own development standard, the daily boresight-to-FRAGO loop named as a life cycle and filed on the BOLO 50 ladder, **in order to** make how the Command builds a written, auditable procedure every project runs the same way.
frago.order: **First use.** The next M or L build runs the loop as written, start to FRAGO, and logs on this sheet where it bent. Second use the same. Two logged uses promote v0.1 to canonical (DOCTRINE 0, Invariant I).
frago.default: Silence: every M or L build from here is a use. The main line logs each one here as a FRAGO. After two, the promotion FRAGO fires without a further call.

items.t: **"Let's fucking table that for now… just remember to put in the BOLO."** Papi tabled the question before it opened.
The question as spoken: the boresight → how-copy → build → FRAGO loop the Command runs every day — is it a design process, or a software life cycle?

Claude's one-line read, logged the same transmission: yes, iterative-incremental development. ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 and 15288 call this the iterative life-cycle model; agile calls it inspect-and-adapt; the Command calls it boresight and FRAGO.

BOLO 50's standards register landed 9/11 (`_0.1_BVX_LEARN/LOCI/standards.locus.md` and `standards.register.md`), but the Command ladder itself — where this standard would file — is still Papi's call per DOPE SHEET 50.

STATE.md and every session note since 9/12 carry the same line — **BOLO 53 tabled** — the Command's own development standard, not started. It has been carried forward untouched across at least three session notes (9/12, 9/12 second session, 9/12 close).

endstate: One document on the ladder names the loop as the Command's iterative-incremental life cycle, stage by stage, each stage a proword.
Every stage cites its outside parent (ISO/IEC 12207 and 15288's iterative model, agile inspect-and-adapt) in one line, no more.
The project flow (BOLO 25) and the logistics front's audits (BOLO 51) point at it as the reference.
Until the open is spoken, it stays tabled and nothing builds.
